Description: Which day's clinic is shown.
Rules and behaviour: Defaults to today.

Description: Six columns in workflow order: To confirm, Confirmed, In the waiting room, With the doctor, Ready to bill, Settled.
Rules and behaviour: A visit appears in one column only.

Description: UHID, name, age and sex, appointment time, doctor and the number to ring.
Rules and behaviour: For a child the guardian's number is shown, because that is who answers.

Description: How many patients sit in each column.
Rings the patient for the confirmation call.
Rules and behaviour: A tel: link, shown on cards awaiting confirmation.

Description: Records that the patient confirmed by telephone.
Rules and behaviour: Moves the visit from Booked to Confirmed.

Description: Records that the patient has reached the clinic.
Rules and behaviour: Stamps the arrival time.

Description: Sends the patient in to the doctor.
Rules and behaviour: Only from the waiting room.

Description: Opens billing for a finished consultation.
Rules and behaviour: Enabled only after the doctor completes the consultation and sets the fee.

Description: Starts a new appointment.
Finds a patient by UHID, mobile number or name.
Given name.
Rules and behaviour: Required.

Description: Family name.
Drives age everywhere else in the system.
Rules and behaviour: Required. Determines whether the patient is treated as paediatric.

Description: Male, female or other.
Rules and behaviour: Required. Growth references are published separately for boys and girls; a child recorded as other cannot be charted.

Description: Primary contact number.
Rules and behaviour: Required. Indian 10-digit format.

Description: Second contact number.
Optional. Not used for appointments.
Postal address.
Recorded once, shown on the chart.
Parent or guardian accompanying the child.
Rules and behaviour: Captured for patients under 18.

Description: The guardian's number.
Rules and behaviour: Becomes the number the clinic actually rings for a child.

Description: Mother, father or other.
Referring doctor or source.
Captured at registration.
Rules and behaviour: Stored on the standing history, so it shows on every future visit.

Description: Clinic-unique identifier, e.g. CEMH-26-00001.
Rules and behaviour: Generated on save from a database sequence, so two receptionists registering at once cannot be given the same number.

Description: Registers the patient and goes straight to booking.
Accepts UHID, mobile number or name.
Rules and behaviour: UHID matching ignores case.

Description: UHID, name, age, sex and mobile number.
Opens the patient's record.
Books for this patient without searching again.
Offered when the search finds nobody.
States plainly that no patient matched.
Rules and behaviour: Never a blank screen.

Description: Chosen by search, or registered on the spot.
Rules and behaviour: Required.

Description: Which doctor the appointment is with.
Rules and behaviour: Required.

Description: Appointment date.
Rules and behaviour: Working days only, and within the booking horizon set for the clinic.

Description: The free times for that doctor on that day.
Rules and behaviour: Only free slots are offered. Slot length comes from clinic settings.

Description: Chief complaint or purpose of the visit.
Marks this as a follow-up rather than a new problem.
Explains in plain words when a slot was taken while the form was open.
Rules and behaviour: The database refuses overlapping bookings outright, so this can happen.

Description: Shows UHID, doctor, date and time.
Patient, UHID, doctor, date and time.
Set by the doctor when finishing the consultation.
Rules and behaviour: Reception cannot change the fee the doctor set.

Description: Any procedure carried out during the visit.
Concession given to the patient.
Consultation plus procedure, less discount.
Rules and behaviour: Calculated, never typed.

Description: Prints the doctor's prescription.
Rules and behaviour: Records that it was printed.

Description: Moves on to taking the money.
What the patient is paying now.
Rules and behaviour: May be less than the total; part payment is supported.

Description: Cash, UPI or card.
Rules and behaviour: Required.

Description: UPI reference or card approval code.
What remains owed after this payment.
Rules and behaviour: The visit stays unsettled while any balance remains.

Description: Unique number carried on the receipt.
Rules and behaviour: Allocated from a database sequence, so two receipts cannot collide.

Description: Prints the receipt for the patient.
Rules and behaviour: Records that it was printed.

Description: Every payment already taken against this visit.
Closes the visit once it is fully settled.
Waiting, in cabin and completed today.
Whoever is in the cabin now, with a link to the chart.
Rules and behaviour: Prefers the in-cabin visit over any later booking for the same patient.

Description: Opens any record by UHID or mobile number.
Rules and behaviour: Not limited to today's list.

Description: Reports that no patient was found rather than failing.
Time, UHID, name, age, reason and status.
Rules and behaviour: In cabin first, then the waiting room in arrival order, then the rest of the day.

Description: Another doctor's patients never appear in this list.
Rules and behaviour: Enforced in the view, not by hiding rows in the page.

Description: Waiting, in cabin, consulted or billed.
Opens the patient's full record.
Name, UHID, age and sex.
Rules and behaviour: Always visible.

Description: Guardian's name and number on the sidebar.
Rules and behaviour: Shown for patients under 18.

Description: Allergies shown prominently on the sidebar.
Rules and behaviour: Never hidden inside a tab; an allergy that must be hunted for gets missed.

Description: Ongoing diagnoses, with the date each began.
Recent visits, latest measurements and attendance.
What the patient reports today.
Findings on examination.
Clinical impression.
Management plan and advice.
Blood pressure, pulse and temperature.
Height in centimetres.
Weight in kilograms.
Computed from height and weight.
Rules and behaviour: Calculated, never typed, so it cannot contradict the measurements beside it.

Description: Recorded and charted for children under three.
Rules and behaviour: The WHO reference for head circumference stops at five years.

Description: Waist circumference.
Puberty staging, I to V.
Mother's and father's heights.
Rules and behaviour: Used for the mid-parental target height.

Description: The child's target height from their parents.
Rules and behaviour: Shown only when both parental heights are known.

Description: Height, weight and BMI for age, plotted over published centile curves.
Rules and behaviour: Offered only for patients under 18. See the Age Rules sheet.

Description: Test name, value, unit, reference range and abnormal flag.
Rules and behaviour: Numeric values are stored separately so results can be trended.

Description: Add a diagnosis, or mark an existing one resolved.
Every prescription issued to this patient.
Ends the consultation, issues the prescription and captures the fee.
Rules and behaviour: Available only while the patient is in the cabin.

Description: Entered by the doctor and passed to reception.
Rules and behaviour: Reception cannot alter it.

Description: Opening any chart is written to the audit trail.
Rules and behaviour: Records who, which patient, from what address and when.

Description: Drug, strength, dose, frequency, duration and instructions.
Rules and behaviour: Lines keep their order, so the printout reads exactly as arranged.

Description: Diet, activity and general advice.
Tests to be done before the next visit.
When the patient should return.
Marks the prescription ready for reception to print.
Rules and behaviour: Generating and printing are recorded separately, so the clinic knows whether a copy actually left the building.

Description: The printed prescription.
Rules and behaviour: Carries the clinic identity, and the doctor's qualification, registration number and signature.

Description: Username, name, email, contact number, role, active and last login.
Creates an account with username, password, email, contact number and role.
Rules and behaviour: Email must be unique.

Description: Doctor, receptionist or patient.
Rules and behaviour: Decides which dashboard the user reaches after signing in.

Description: Minimum ten characters.
Rules and behaviour: Common passwords, all-numeric passwords and passwords resembling the username are refused.

Description: Sets a new password for a user who is locked out.
Disables an account without deleting it.
Rules and behaviour: Never delete: the audit trail must keep pointing at a real person.

Description: Show only doctors, receptionists or patients.
A role check runs in every view that reaches a patient record.
Rules and behaviour: Typing a URL for another role's screen returns 403, not the page.

Description: Medical council registration.
Rules and behaviour: Printed on the prescription.

Description: Degrees, as they should appear on the prescription.
Area of practice.
Uploaded signature image.
Rules and behaviour: Appears on printed prescriptions.

Description: Timestamp, user, role, action, patient UHID, IP address and page.
Viewed, created, updated, printed, login, logout and failed login.
Rules and behaviour: A failed login records the username tried, never the password submitted.

Description: Everything one member of staff did.
Everyone who opened one patient's record.
Rules and behaviour: The question the clinic may one day have to answer to a patient.

Description: Period covered.
Entries can never be edited or deleted.
Rules and behaviour: Refused at the database layer and in the admin, even for a superuser.

Description: Guardian name, relation and phone number are captured at registration.
Rules and behaviour: Not asked for an adult patient.

Description: The guardian's number becomes the contact number for confirmation calls.
Rules and behaviour: For an adult, their own mobile is used.

Description: Height, weight and BMI plotted against published centile curves.
Rules and behaviour: The tab is not offered for an adult, and the URL is refused, not merely hidden.

Description: WHO Child Growth Standards 2006.
Rules and behaviour: Exact centile and z-score, computed from published LMS parameters.

Description: IAP 2015 revised charts for Indian children.
Rules and behaviour: IAP publishes the curves only, so the child is placed in the band between two printed centiles, with an SDS interpolated between them.

Description: No growth chart.
Rules and behaviour: CDC covers 18 to 20 years and is used, labelled, only where a patient is still under the paediatric limit.

Description: No centile or SDS is invented past the outermost printed curve.
Rules and behaviour: The band is stated, and a z-score from a reference that can still compute one is shown alongside, labelled with its source.

Description: Thinness, normal, overweight or obesity from the IAP adult-equivalent lines.
Rules and behaviour: The 23 and 27 adult-equivalent cut-offs, which are age and sex specific: 15.7 at five years, 23.2 at eighteen.

Description: BMI is calculated and shown, with no childhood banding.
Rules and behaviour: The paediatric cut-offs must never be applied to an adult, nor the adult 25 and 30 to a child.

Description: Recorded and charted.
Rules and behaviour: The WHO reference stops at five years, so the curve stops there too.

Description: Puberty stage I to V recorded at the visit.
Rules and behaviour: Not asked for an adult.

Description: Mother's and father's heights, giving the mid-parental target height.
Rules and behaviour: Shown only when both are known.

Description: The boundary is a clinic setting, currently 18 years.
Rules and behaviour: Changing it changes which patients are offered the growth chart.
